newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris court jails Moslem militants, five held.
newsitem.headline: Paris court jails Moslem militants, five held.

text.p: A Paris court on Thursday sentenced 26 members of an alleged militant Moslem support network to up to eight years in jail on charges of ordering attacks in Morocco, including one in which two Spaniards died in 1994.
Abdelilah Ziyad, a 38-year-old Moroccan who admitted setting up the network to undermine King Hassan II, was sent down for eight years.
A second Moroccan ringleader, Mohamed Zinedine, 36, was given a eight-year sentence in his absence.
Djamel Lounici, a 34-year-old Algerian Moslem fundamentalist currently being held in Italy, was sentenced to five years.

As the sentences were announced, police said they detained five people in Islamic circles in the Lyon region in a probe into a wave of bomb attacks in which eight people died last year. The attacks were blamed on Algerian Moslem rebels.
They said the five were detained for questioning during routine checks and were not connected to last month's rush-hour bomb attack on a Paris commuter train which killed four people.
That attack had taken place just before the trial of the Moslem network opened, spurring fears of revenge attacks on France by fundamentalist guerrillas.
The court sentenced 26 defendents to between one and eight years and threw out the cases against another six, who had already been convicted in Morocco, on a technicality.

Prosecutors had requested jail terms of up to 10 years for the 34 accused, 13 of whom were being tried in absentia. The accused are believed to have been recruited by the ringleaders between 1988 and 1994 in the Paris area, Orleans and the eastern town of Besancon.
Police said the network was dismantled after four guerrilla attacks in Morocco in 1994 including the shooting of the Spanish tourists during a robbery at a Marrakesh hotel.
A Moroccan court has sentenced three people to death over the attack, including two French youths of North African origin.
The other attacks failed. They targetted Jews in Casablanca, police in Fes and nude bathers in Tangiers.
